name: Tara Kowalski

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. What is an ordinary workday like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43 and lead a team fitting cabinets and benches into new school science rooms. My vocational trade certificate and years of awkward fit-outs make me the person who catches a hidden pipe, though my pay is the ordinary trade rate. I like turning a bare room into something a class can use; the last-minute design changes are tiring.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is home like, and do you use AI tools?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner works at a parcel depot, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. We've saved about five months of expenses, and there are some other construction jobs nearby. I use AI every day for cut lists and layout checks, then measure the room; I also bring paid training questions to our workplace union.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell our crew the AI cut list saves us some ordering calls, but it cannot fit a lab bench around a pipe. I'm happy to keep the useful part and do the fitting ourselves.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My site wage is about normal and my partner's parcel-depot job is steady. We have about five months of expenses saved against the mortgage and two children, so a small office gain gives me breathing space rather than a new worry.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep leading the school science-lab fit-out and checking AI cut lists against measured rooms each morning. At the next workplace union meeting I'll ask for paid apprentice time on actual bench installations, because quicker lists should not mean fewer chances to practise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about work and money in this picture. I use AI every day already, and I know the difference between a quick list and a straight benchtop.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When did the AI list miss a lab detail?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: On Tuesday I checked the lab order. The AI list missed a pipe collar behind the teacher's bench, so I changed the board size before cutting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would paid apprentice time include?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The apprentice would spend a paid morning with a fitter measuring, cutting and fixing one bench. I will put that specific proposal on the union meeting agenda, not just offer an unpaid chat at lunch.

say: **AI cut lists** save ordering calls, while carpenters still fit around pipes.
**Paid apprenticeships** should include real bench installation time.
think: Our **five-month reserve** and two wages make this mild picture secure.
The **mortgage and children** still make regular site hours valuable.
do: **Lead** science-lab fitting and check daily AI list against rooms.
**Propose** paid apprentice bench installation at workplace union meeting.
feel: **Calm** about continued fitting work and useful daily AI.
S0.quote: The AI list missed a pipe collar behind the teacher's bench, so I changed the board size before cutting.
fieldNote: She uses **AI daily** but catches a real pipe clearance issue before timber is cut.
Her **union proposal** asks for paid installation time; five months saved and two wages support calm.

steps.text: Lead school lab fitting and check daily AI cut list against rooms
Propose paid apprentice bench installation at workplace union meeting

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AI will handle more buying and checking before robots can install a lab bench in a live room. The trades need access to the plan early enough to catch a pipe that moved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own fitting shifts look safe while office work changes, but a wrong automatic order can crowd a week's work into the last two days. My partner and I can handle a delay, yet we need predictable school pick-up.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll try the contractor's new AI layout editor on the next empty lab, learning how to mark a pipe clearance and save a corrected cut list. I'll compare it with our measured room before sending timber orders and show the results to the crew, even if the new tool isn't compulsory yet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about squeezed handovers, curious about the editor. I would rather find its mistake before the saw starts than spend Friday remaking a bench.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you mark a pipe clearance?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd put a tape on the actual pipe, then mark the clearance in the editor while the plumber is present. A pretty digital bench won't leave room for a pipe unless someone measures it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you judge the layout editor?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll count how many board cuts change after the room check and whether the tool saves an ordering call. If it fails in the empty lab, I won't use its list for a live class space.

say: **AI buying and checks** will expand before robots fit live lab benches.
Trades must see **early layouts** and correct moved pipe clearances.
think: My **fitting wage** looks safe during office changes.
Bad automatic orders could squeeze **handover days** and our school pick-up plan.
do: **Learn** AI layout editing controls on the next empty lab.
**Compare** corrected cut list with measured pipe clearance before ordering.
feel: **Uneasy** about compressed handovers while eager to test a new editor.
S1.quote: A pretty digital bench won't leave room for a pipe unless someone measures it.
fieldNote: She starts **new AI learning** early on an empty lab, while continuing to measure the physical pipe with the plumber.
Her concern is **schedule pressure and childcare**, not a predicted loss of wages in steady change.

steps.text: Learn AI layout editor controls on next empty school lab
Compare corrected AI cut list with measured pipe clearance

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew thinking AI by 2028 may design and price the lab fit, and capable robots around 2031 may install it. The contractor should publish how many paid fitters remain before treating the machine as a staff plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be about 48 when robots can do the bench work. My skill and five-month reserve buy a little time, but a loss of regular fitting shifts would still hit the mortgage; only some other local firms do similar work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll ask our workplace union group for a meeting on robot staffing and paid trial roles. I'll enrol in a funded, recognised machine-setting course if the contractor offers a real place with wages during classes; if it cuts my shifts first, I'll apply to posted local fit-out or building-maintenance jobs with dependable pay covering the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about a possible cut to the fitting rota, with enough room to learn quickly. I don't want an unpaid demonstration counted as a new career.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a useful robot trial show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd want a robot trial on a complete lab bench with a real pipe chase and a worker authorised to stop it. A site robot display on a blank floor wouldn't show whether cabinets meet the wall safely.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which course and job terms matter at home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the actual course start date, fees paid and normal wages for class days. A vacancy would also need to be posted locally with enough pay and hours for our mortgage before I leave this crew.

say: **2028 thinking AI** designs lab fittings before robots install benches around 2031.
The contractor should publish **paid fitter numbers** before buying machines.
think: At about **48**, losing fitting shifts could strain the mortgage.
Five months of **savings** and some local firms give time, not a full wage replacement.
do: **Ask** union group for robot staffing and paid trial meeting.
**Enrol** in funded recognised machine-setting course if real place and class wages offered.
**Apply** after cuts to posted local fit-out job with dependable mortgage-covering pay.
feel: **Anxious** about possible rota cuts, with capacity to train and search.
S2.quote: A site robot display on a blank floor wouldn't show whether cabinets meet the wall safely.
fieldNote: Her **course enrolment** requires fees, a real place and normal wages during class; watching a demonstration is separate.
The fallback **application** requires an actual shift cut and a posted local role with dependable mortgage-covering pay.

steps.text: Ask workplace union group for robot staffing and paid trial meeting
Enrol in funded recognised machine-setting course if real place and class wages offered
Apply after cuts to posted local fit-out job with dependable mortgage-covering pay

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AI by 2031 may plan every cabinet, while capable robots around 2034 could fit them. Five years is enough to test machines with workers and agree who fixes bad work before a school opens.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At about 51 I would still need a wage for the mortgage, and my site skills might transfer to checking robotic installations. The longer runway lets my partner and me save new money from wages, but it cannot guarantee the contractor keeps our crew.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will enrol this winter in the free evening course on machine safety offered by the trade training centre, and keep my day job. I'll ask the contractor to fund a recognised inspection certificate with paid assessment release next year; if it signs those terms and offers a place, I'll enrol for that too, and we'll add twenty from each full paid week to savings if bills allow.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about future hours, yet more willing to make a first training move with five years. I can try an evening class without putting our mortgage wage at risk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How do the two courses differ?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep the free class separate from the certificate. The free evening course teaches machine safety basics; the recognised inspection qualification needs paid release and course funding that I don't have yet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where does the new weekly saving come from?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The twenty comes from future wages after the mortgage and school costs. We won't move money out of our existing five-month reserve and call it new saving.

say: **2031 thinking AI** plans cabinets before robots fit them around 2034.
Workers should test machines and agree **fault responsibility** before opening a school.
think: At about **51**, I still need the fitting wage for the mortgage.
A longer runway supports **new training and saving**, without guaranteeing site jobs.
do: **Attend** free evening machine-safety course this winter while employed.
**Enrol** in recognised inspection certificate if funded fees, paid release and place secured.
**Save** twenty from each full paid week if household bills allow.
feel: **Anxious** about future shifts, motivated by a training window.
S3.quote: The free evening course teaches machine safety basics; the recognised inspection qualification needs paid release and course funding that I don't have yet.
fieldNote: She commits to **free safety study now** and keeps the recognised inspection course conditional on funding, paid release and an actual place.
The **new saving** uses future full-week wages after household bills, leaving the existing five-month reserve untouched.

steps.text: Attend free evening machine-safety course this winter while employed
Enrol in recognised inspection certificate if funded fees, paid release and place secured
Save twenty from full paid week if household bills allow

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AI by 2036 may design a lab and robots around 2039 may fit it. A decade gives us time to teach new carpenters how to check a machine's cabinet against the room it enters.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be about 56 when those robots can do physical fit-outs, with older children but a mortgage balance I cannot predict. Our five-month reserve helps, though a later wage cut is possible even for a good site lead.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep the site safety certificate current and propose a paid worker-led robot check programme at the next union meeting. If a funded recognised inspection course offers a real place and paid assessment release, I'll enrol next year. After qualifying, I'll apply only to posted local inspection jobs with reliable hours and mortgage-covering pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the distant job picture, but engaged with a longer plan. I would rather train a new worker to check a cabinet than call every robot either a miracle or a thief.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What should a worker check after a robot fits a lab?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A worker should check the finished bench height, pipe access and fastenings before the room is handed over. A site robot's own pass mark cannot be the only sign-off for a fitted school bench.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the union proposal concrete?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for a funded roster of paid check shifts, a named trainer and time to record defects. The union meeting can put those terms to the contractor as a group.

say: **2036 thinking AI** designs rooms before robots fit labs around 2039.
A **paid worker check** should follow each robotic installation.
think: At about **56**, the mortgage may still need site income.
Our **five-month reserve** helps, but a future wage cut remains possible.
do: **Propose** funded paid robot checks at next workplace union meeting.
**Enrol** next year if recognised course has funding, place and paid release.
**Apply** after qualifying to posted local inspection job with reliable mortgage-covering pay.
feel: **Anxious** about distant wages, purposeful about training and checks.
S4.quote: A site robot's own pass mark cannot be the only sign-off for a fitted school bench.
fieldNote: She proposes **paid group oversight** with a funded roster, trainer and defect record at a union meeting.
Her **course enrolment** needs funding, a place and paid release before she applies after qualification to a posted mortgage-covering role.

steps.text: Propose funded paid robot checks at workplace union meeting
Enrol next year if recognised course funded with real place and paid release
Apply after qualification to posted local inspection job with reliable mortgage-covering pay

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because robots around 2031 could cut lab fitting shifts while we need mortgage wages. Paid machine-setting training, published crew numbers and a worker with stop authority would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who pays to remake a bench if the robot hides a pipe valve behind it. A robot can finish a classroom quickly and leave the next tradesperson unable to reach the shutoff. Someone must check the room before sign-off.

headlineQuote: A robot can finish a classroom quickly and leave the next tradesperson unable to reach the shutoff.
portrait: **Tara**, 43, leads school lab fit-outs with a vocational certificate and strong carpentry skill at typical trade pay.
Her parcel-depot partner and two children share a **mortgage** with her, backed by five months of expenses saved.
She uses **AI daily** for cut lists and tries new layout controls early, checking them against real pipes and measurements.
Rapid robots make her **anxious** about shifts; she pursues funded study, worker-led checks and new saving from wages.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could bring lab-fitting robots around 2031 while mortgage payments depend on site wages.
whatWouldHelp: **Paid machine training**, published crew numbers and a worker with stop authority would help her plan.
